The Iwaidja are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Cobourg Peninsula in the north of the Northern Territory. Today they are also known as the Arrarrkbi, since survivors of neighbouring groups such as the Garig and Marrgu joined them after British colonisation.

For generations Makassan trepang fishers from Sulawesi camped on this coast each wet season, and words and goods passed between them. Britain tried twice to settle the peninsula: Fort Wellington at Raffles Bay from 1827 to 1829, and the Victoria settlement at Port Essington from 1838 to 1849. All failed, but they brought disease.

Their neighbours were the Amurdak, Kunbarlang and Gaagudju.
